legend: In a peripheral blood smear, the leukaemic cells are very similar to normal large granular lymphocytes in this case (Giemsa) (<<30763>>). The leukaemic cells in the bone marrow show basophilic cytoplasm, and nuclei with more condensed chromatin and distinct nucleoli. Azurophilic granules can be observed in the cytoplasm (Giemsa) (<<30764>>). Nuclear pleomorphism and haemophagocytosis are apparent (Giemsa) (<<30767>>).
